event_date_basis: Confirmed independently today (2026-09-18) on all three fetched pages, not merely copied from the exploratory record. (1) Mistral's post prints 'September 16, 2026' under its title with byline 'By Mistral and Mozilla'. (2) Mozilla's partnership post prints 'September 16, 2026' under its own title. (3) The August Smart Window post carries a stacked update block headed 'Update on September 16, 2026'. All three are dates, not timestamps -- mistral.ai gives no time of day at all, and no clock time is written into the article for this reason. Mistral's forward-looking market language ('expected to follow later this year') and Mozilla's ('planning additional European expansion later this year') are not dates and are written in the article exactly as the vendors phrased them, not converted into a deadline.

sourcing_notes: Re-verified independently on 2026-09-18 (this is the writer's own fetch, done after reading the 2026-09-18 exploratory research record at docs/news-2026-batch-4/research/ai-news-firefox-smart-window-mistral-20260916.json, and used to check that record rather than just copy it). curl -sL -A "Mokaair-editorial" against all three URLs, no email, name or personal data in any header, query string or form: https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-x-mozilla/ -> HTTP 200 / 243,456 bytes (exact match with the exploratory record); https://blog.mozilla.org/en/firefox/mozilla-mistral-partnership/ -> HTTP 200 / 69,692 bytes (the exploratory record logged 69,671 bytes for the same URL earlier the same day -- a 21-byte difference on a live blog page, not evidence of a different document); https://blog.mozilla.org/en/firefox/firefox-smart-window/ -> HTTP 200 / 71,906 bytes (exact match). All three bodies were read in full. Every verbatim_quote below was re-derived today with a script searching the freshly saved HTML, not copied from the exploratory record, specifically to catch a transcription error before it reached the article; none was found. Two checks worth recording. First, the string 'Mistral Small 4' does appear on mistral.ai's page, but only inside a sitewide product-navigation card (class names group-hover/link:translate-x-8, font-mistral) that lists Mistral's product line, not inside the announcement's own prose -- this confirms, rather than contradicts, that Mistral's post never names a version in its own words. Second, a raw case-insensitive search for Taiwan/Japan/Korea returns one hit each on both Mozilla pages, but every hit sits inside a <select> element listing all world countries (a sitewide contact- or newsletter-form region picker), e.g. '<option value="tw">Taiwan</option>', not in the article body -- confirmed by reading the surrounding HTML before treating the negative ('the article text does not name Taiwan') as safe to write. The misspelling 'Mistal's scientific innovations' (curly apostrophe, U+2019) was located in the body text and is kept verbatim in the record; the correctly spelled CEO quote lower on the same page is recorded separately. mistral.ai/news carries no machine-readable date anywhere in its markup, only the human string 'September 16, 2026' under the title. No news outlet, aggregator or search snippet was used for any fact.

verified_facts.fact: Mistral published its announcement on 2026-09-16 with a joint byline.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: September 16, 2026 By Mistral and Mozilla

verified_facts.fact: What was announced, in Mistral's own opening sentence: a partnership with Mozilla for people using AI to browse.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Today, we are announcing a partnership with Mozilla to bring privacy, control and choice to people using AI to browse online.

verified_facts.fact: Mistral names no model version in its own post, only 'Mistral models', unnumbered.

not_said: Taiwan is not named by either company, and no Asian market is named at all. Re-checked independently on all three pages on 2026-09-18: the only markets named anywhere in the article prose are France, North America / the US and Canada, and the United Kingdom and Germany. A raw substring search returns 'Taiwan', 'Japan' and 'Korea' once or twice on each Mozilla page, but every hit sits inside the sitewide newsletter country-selector <select> (e.g. '<option value="tw">Taiwan</option>'); mistral.ai contains none of the three strings at all. Confirmed by inspecting the surrounding HTML. The article must write that neither company's announcement names Taiwan or any Asian market, and must not write that Smart Window is unavailable in Taiwan. CORRECTED BY THE INDEPENDENT FACTCHECK: the reason is NOT that Mozilla never enumerates its markets -- the August post does say 'currently available in English to people in the U.S. and Canada' -- the reason is that neither company publishes an EXCLUSION list, and Mozilla's own sentence points anyone outside those markets at a notification sign-up rather than saying a country is ruled out. Mistral separately claims the partnership reaches Firefox users 'worldwide', which is one more reason not to convert the silence into a denial.

No release channel and no Firefox version number. Neither page says which Firefox version contains Smart Window. CORRECTED BY THE INDEPENDENT FACTCHECK: the August post does tell a reader outside the named markets what to do -- 'you can sign up to be notified when it is' -- and links firefox.com/smart-window (and .../?view=enable), so the earlier 'neither page says how a user checks whether they have it' was too strong.

No language list beyond French and English. Mistral claims fine-tuning on regional languages and dialects but names none. CORRECTED BY THE INDEPENDENT FACTCHECK: Mozilla names TWO languages across the three pages, not one -- French in the partnership post and English in the August post ('currently available in English'). Traditional Chinese support is not addressed on any of the three pages. SECOND ROUND, 2026-09-18: the same country-selector trap applies to Chinese as to Taiwan -- a raw search for '正體中文' hits both Mozilla pages, every time inside the sitewide newsletter LANGUAGE picker (alongside Deutsch, Español, Русский), never in the prose; the Latin string 'Chinese' is absent from all three pages. The article's negative was therefore scoped to the prose ('三頁正文都沒有提到') so that it is true at the string level too.
No price, and no statement about whether Smart Window will remain free.
No detail behind 'zero data retention' or 'by default': no duration, scope, audit mechanism, or published policy document is linked from either page.
No benchmark, score or evaluation methodology behind Mozilla's claim that it evaluated Mistral Small 4's performance.
No enumeration of the 'multitude of other AI models' Firefox users can otherwise choose.
No commercial terms: no statement of who pays whom, or how long the arrangement runs.
No user numbers, adoption figures or beta participant count on any of the three pages.
No mention of any regulator, competition authority or the EU Digital Markets Act, despite both posts being framed around competition and user choice.

editorial_brief: 讀者是用 Firefox、或只是好奇為何每個瀏覽器都在加入 AI 助理的台灣一般讀者，不是開發者或企業採購。這則消息在時程上碰不到台灣：具名的市場只有法國、北美、以及預計稍後跟進的英國與德國，讀者現在用不到。文章的價值因此不在「馬上能用」，而在兩件可以搬到其他情境的事：第一，這是今年很清楚的一個例子，說明瀏覽器把 AI 模型當成可以抽換的插槽，而不是固定寫死的引擎——Mozilla 自己說使用者仍可以選別的模型，另外還花錢跟 Exa 買了網路檢索能力；第二，這是一次乾淨的讀公告練習，因為兩家一手來源同一天發布、對同一件事寫出不完全相同的版本。核心是不要幫兩家公司做出結論：Mistral 的市場句與 Mozilla 的市場句分開印，各自標明出處，表格是這個分歧最自然的落腳處。第二個要顧好的地方是「沒說的」要寫成沒說，不能寫成「不行」——台灣與亞洲完全沒有出現在兩份公告的正文裡，這是「官方沒有提到」，不是「官方說台灣不能用」，兩者是本文一定要分清楚的差異。刻意不談的範圍：任何跟其他瀏覽器內建 AI 助理的比較、開放權重模型的技術定義（不是這次的主題）、任何競爭法或市場獨占的角度（兩家公司都沒有點名任何對手）、本站沒有做過的手動測試心得。
must_not_write: Do not pick one company's market list as the answer; print Mistral's and Mozilla's versions side by side, each attributed to its publisher.
Do not write that Smart Window is unavailable in Taiwan. Write that neither company's announcement names Taiwan or any Asian market.
Do not attribute the model name 'Mistral Small 4' to Mistral; that wording is Mozilla's. Mistral's own post says only 'Mistral models'.
Do not write that Smart Window is powered by Mistral, full stop; Mozilla says users can still choose other models, and separately names Exa for web retrieval.
Do not date Smart Window itself to 2026-09-16; it was announced 2026-08-18 and had already been in beta for months.

Do not present 'zero data retention' or 'not saved by default' as a verified, documented policy; they are the vendors' own statements, with no linked policy document and no explanation of what 'by default' means.
Do not name Google, or any other company, as the target of Mozilla's 'Big Tech-default browser ecosystems' or 'global tech monopolies' language; Mozilla names nobody.
Do not mention the EU Digital Markets Act or any regulator; neither company does.
Do not claim Traditional Chinese support at any level; Mistral names no language, Mozilla names only French.
Do not write that the site tried or tested Smart Window; nobody at this site has used it.
Do not quote 'Mistal's scientific innovations' as if it were a normal spelling without flagging that the misspelling is the source's own.
Do not draw any logo, wordmark or UI screenshot in the hero or diagram, and do not put a number on the artwork that the body text does not also state.
live_data_warnings: https://blog.mozilla.org/en/firefox/firefox-smart-window/ is a live document: it is an August post carrying a stacked 'Update on September 16, 2026' block, and Mozilla can add further dated updates to the same URL without changing it. Anyone re-checking this article later should look for additional update blocks rather than assume today's snapshot is final.

mistral.ai/news exposes no feed and no ISO timestamps anywhere in its markup, only human-readable date strings such as 'September 16, 2026'; a later re-check of this article should not assume an article URL can be guessed (a guess at /news/mistral-mozilla-firefox returns a soft 404 that still serves a full-size page) or that a machine-readable date will be available.

The two byte counts recorded for https://blog.mozilla.org/en/firefox/mozilla-mistral-partnership/ (69,671 bytes in the same-day exploratory record, 69,692 bytes in this writer's own later fetch) differ by 21 bytes; treated here as the same live page at two moments, not as evidence of two different documents. THIRD DATA POINT from the independent factcheck's own fetch later on 2026-09-18: 69,671 bytes again, i.e. back to the exploratory record's figure. The page oscillates by a few bytes between requests, so byte count is a fetch-success test here and nothing more -- it must not be used as a version identifier.

mistral.ai/news/mistral-x-mozilla/ DOES carry a JSON-LD NewsArticle block, contrary to the note above that says the page has no machine-readable date anywhere in its markup. The block is unusable rather than absent: both 'datePublished' and 'dateModified' are the literal placeholder string 'YYYY-MM-DD', and its '@id' and 'mainEntityOfPage' point at https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-mozilla-partnership, a URL different from the canonical one that actually serves the post. The only real date on the page remains the human string 'September 16, 2026'.

mistral.ai/news/mistral-x-mozilla/ has two different titles and a later re-checker will meet both. The <title>, og:title and twitter:title all read 'Mistral x Mozilla: Private, Multilingual AI Browsing' (recorded in sources[] above), while the on-page <h1> and the JSON-LD 'headline' both read 'Mistral and Mozilla are bringing open, private and multilingual AI to your web browser'. The article's running text was changed by the independent factcheck so that it no longer presents either string as the post's headline.

factcheck.method: Did not take part in the writing. All three sources[] URLs re-fetched today with curl -sL -A "Mokaair-editorial" -- no email, name or personal data in any UA, header, query string or form -- and all three bodies read in full. 94 claims checked one by one: title, description, both opening paragraphs, the 4 summary sentences, every sentence of the 11 body paragraphs, all 5 FAQ answers, the callout, all 16 table cells plus the caption, the diagram caption and the record's own 4 diagram nodes and hero_label. All 20 pre-existing verbatim_quote values were re-derived by script against the freshly saved HTML after Unicode normalisation: 20/20 exact, 0 misses. Every new quote added below was verified the same way before being written. No URL outside sources[] was used to support any sentence in the article; the sitewide navigation, the JSON-LD block and the newsletter country <select> were read only to test negative claims. checked_on was NOT moved: the writer's 2026-09-18 is the day they read the sources and is also the day of this re-check, and it is consistent across the pack's three sources, this record, the second paragraph, the table caption and the diagram caption.
edits_to_the_pack: THE BIGGEST ONE, corrected in 9 places: the article called this a model swap ('換模型', '改用', '換上', '模型換人'). Mozilla's own sentence is 'Mistral Small 4 is coming to Firefox Smart Window beta ... becoming a NEW AI model for Smart Window users in the US and Canada', and the same post adds 'Firefox users can still choose from a multitude of other AI models'. The Mozilla Connect thread Mozilla itself links calls it 'mistral-as-a-new-model'. Changed everywhere to an added option ('多一個模型選項' / '多了 Mistral 的模型'): paragraph 1, summary sentences 2 and 3, the section-1 heading, section 1 paragraphs 1 and 3, section 2 paragraph 1, section 3 paragraph 3, FAQ 2, the table's Mozilla row, and the record's own diagram node.

Deleted the invented start date '從 9 月 16 日起，美國與加拿大的 Smart Window 使用者將改用 Mistral 的模型'. Mozilla publishes no start date for the model; it writes 'is coming to'. Replaced with Mozilla's own tense and the 'a new AI model' wording, attributed.

'Smart Window 在 2026 年 8 月 18 日已經推出' was wrong in 4 places (paragraph 1, summary 3, section 1 paragraph 3, FAQ 2). The 8/18 post says 'We've spent the last several months building and testing Smart Window in beta with our community' and 'Today, we're adding new capabilities' -- 8/18 added capabilities to something that already existed. Rewritten as what Mozilla wrote on that date; the article's central point (Smart Window predates 9/16) survives and is now correctly sourced.

'Mozilla 執行長 Anthony Enzor-DeMeo' -> 'Mozilla Corporation 執行長'. Both pages print 'CEO of Mozilla Corporation'; the Mozilla Foundation and the Mozilla Corporation are separate legal entities and neither source supports the shortened form. Also changed '在公告中被引述' to '在兩份公告中都被引述', which is verifiable: the same quote appears on mistral.ai as 'Anthony Enzor-DeMeo, CEO, Mozilla Corporation'.

Added Mozilla's own answer to the default/off-switch question, which the draft left out although it is the reader's first practical question: 'Smart Window is optional. You choose when to use it, what browsing context it can use ..., and which AI model you want to use' and 'Firefox's AI Controls gives you one place to manage Smart Window, including turning it off entirely.' Added to section 3 and to FAQ 3.

Added Mozilla's availability sentence to the Taiwan section and FAQ 1: 'It's currently available in English to people in the U.S. and Canada. If it's not available where you are yet, you can sign up to be notified when it is.' The draft's guard ('不是「台灣用不到」') is kept verbatim -- the addition is an inclusion list, not an exclusion list -- but hiding a first-party availability statement from a reader asking '台灣用得到嗎' was the wrong kind of caution.

Scoped the model-name negative to the announcement's prose: 'Mistral 自己的公告只提到「Mistral 的模型」' -> '公告正文', with the check written out ('以 2026 年 9 月 18 日查核，「Mistral Small 4」在該頁只出現在全站的產品選單，不在公告內文'). The string does occur twice on mistral.ai, both times inside the sitewide 'Latest models' navigation card. Same fix in the table's Mistral row and in FAQ 3.
'Mozilla 這次只點名法文' -> 'Mozilla 點名的語言只有法文與英文（8 月原文寫的是目前以英文提供）'. The August post names English, so 'only French' was a false negative.
'已經變成' -> '已經從…擴大到…'. Mozilla writes 'competition HAS EXPANDED FROM "which AI model is best?" TO ...' -- expansion, not replacement.

'Smart Window 正式在法國推出' -> '「開始在法國推出」'. The update block says 'is now rolling out in France' and 'People in France WILL BE ABLE TO download and try the Smart Window beta in French'. '正式' overstated a beta rollout.
Taiwan negative scoped and dated: '以查證範圍來說' -> '以 2026 年 9 月 18 日查核的這三頁正文來說'; the language paragraph's '兩份公告' -> '三頁', since the negative was tested on all three sources.

Table: Mozilla's forward-looking cell gained the qualifier Mozilla actually prints ('「規劃」今年稍後歐洲擴展'); the August-update row's '無新增計畫' -> '更新區塊未再提', because the August page does carry a 'What's next' section (browsing journeys, form filling) even though the update block does not.

The data paragraph and FAQ 4 now say what the reader actually wants to know is missing: neither page states whether the conversation is sent to Mistral's servers for processing. '兩份公告' -> '三個來源頁面' in the same sentence, since the absence of a linked policy document was verified on all three (every <a> in all three article bodies was listed; there is no privacy, data or AI-Controls document among them).

Removed the English title 〈Mistral x Mozilla: Private, Multilingual AI Browsing〉 from paragraph 2. It is the page's <title>/og:title, but the on-page <h1> and the JSON-LD headline read differently, so presenting it as the post's headline was not supportable. sources[] keeps it as the page title.

Four purely editorial trims to stay inside the 3,000-character budget after the additions ('讀者可以自己比較', '或其他常用軟體', and two shortenings inside sentences added by this factcheck). No qualifier, hedge or attribution was removed to make room.
